sentences.text: Yangchuanosaurus was a large and powerful carnivore that walked on two large, muscular legs.
It possessed a bony crest on its nose and multiple horns and crests, similar to Ceratosaurus.
The animal possessed a long tail that reached half the total body length.
Its feet featured a small dewclaw on the first digit, while the three outer toes bore weight and each held a large claw.
The animal may have reached a length of up to 10.8 meters and weighed up to 3.4 metric tons.
The type specimen had a skull measuring 82 cm in length and a total body length estimated at 8 meters.
The type specimen was discovered in June 1977 by a construction worker building the Shangyou Reservoir Dam.
Dong et al. named the species Yangchuanosaurus shangyouensis in 1978 based on a complete skull and skeleton found near Yongchuan, Sichuan.
Yangchuanosaurus was the largest predator in its ecosystem, sharing the Upper Shaximiao Formation with sauropods like Mamenchisaurus and stegosaurs like Tuojiangosaurus.
It was a fast runner that used three-toed feet and hands with sharp, curved claws to grab prey like sauropods Mamenchisaurus and Omeisaurus.
Yangchuanosaurus belongs to the family Metriacanthosauridae.
The genus Yangchuanosaurus was described by Dong et al. in 1978.
A 2012 analysis identified Yangchuanosaurus as the most basal known metriacanthosaurid and the only one outside the Metriacanthosaurinae subfamily.
A 2012 phylogenetic study by Carrano, Benson, and Sampson concluded that the two named species of Yangchuanosaurus are actually the same species.
Gregory S. Paul suggested in 1988 that Yangchuanosaurus should be considered a synonym of Metriacanthosaurus, but this view was not supported by later research.
Yangchuanosaurus lived in China during the Middle Jurassic to Late Jurassic periods, specifically from the Bathonian to Tithonian stages.
The type specimen of Yangchuanosaurus dates to the Oxfordian stage of the Late Jurassic, approximately 161.2 to 157.3 million years ago.

The classification of Y.? hepingensis is debated, with some paleontologists questioning its identity within Sinraptor while others, like Rauhut and colleagues, place it within Yangchuanosaurus based on phylogenetic analysis.
It is debated whether CV 00214 and Szechuanosaurus zigongensis are the same species, as Carrano et al. noted they lack shared unique traits and come from different geological formations.
The assignment of Szechuanosaurus zigongensis to Yangchuanosaurus is considered questionable by Rauhut and colleagues despite its close relationship to Y. shangyouensis.
